info.name: Return AP channel utilization over time for a device or network client

params.name: t0
params.description: The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 31 days from today.

params.name: t1
params.description: The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 31 days after t0.

params.name: timespan
params.description: The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 31 days. The default is 7 days.

params.name: resolution
params.description: The time resolution in seconds for returned data. The valid resolutions are: 600, 1200, 3600, 14400, 86400. The default is 86400.

params.name: autoResolution
params.description: Automatically select a data resolution based on the given timespan; this overrides the value specified by the 'resolution' parameter. The default setting is false.

params.name: clientId
params.description: Filter results by network client to return per-device, per-band AP channel utilization metrics inner joined by the queried client's connection history.

params.name: deviceSerial
params.description: Filter results by device to return AP channel utilization metrics for the queried device; either :band or :clientId must be jointly specified.

params.name: apTag
params.description: Filter results by AP tag to return AP channel utilization metrics for devices labeled with the given tag; either :clientId or :deviceSerial must be jointly specified.

items.docs: Return AP channel utilization over time for a device or network client

info.name: List the wireless connectivity events for a client within a network in the timespan.

params.name: perPage
params.description: The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 1000.

params.name: startingAfter
params.description: A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.

params.name: endingBefore
params.description: A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.

params.name: sortOrder
params.description: Sorted order of entries. Order options are 'ascending' and 'descending'. Default is 'ascending'.

params.name: t0
params.description: The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 31 days from today.

params.name: t1
params.description: The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 31 days after t0.

params.name: timespan
params.description: The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 31 days. The default is 1 day.

params.name: types
params.description: A list of event types to include. If not specified, events of all types will be returned. Valid types are 'assoc', 'disassoc', 'auth', 'deauth', 'dns', 'dhcp', 'roam', 'connection' and/or 'sticky'.

params.name: band
params.description: Filter results by band. Valid bands are '2.4', '5' or '6'.

params.name: ssidNumber
params.description: Filter results by SSID. If not specified, events for all SSIDs will be returned.

params.name: includedSeverities
params.description: A list of severities to include. If not specified, events of all severities will be returned. Valid severities are 'good', 'info', 'warn' and/or 'bad'.

params.name: deviceSerial
params.description: Filter results by an AP's serial number.

items.docs: List the wireless connectivity events for a client within a network in the timespan.

info.name: Return the latency history for a client

params.name: t0
params.description: The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 791 days from today.

params.name: t1
params.description: The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 791 days after t0.

params.name: timespan
params.description: The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 791 days. The default is 1 day.

params.name: resolution
params.description: The time resolution in seconds for returned data. The valid resolutions are: 86400. The default is 86400.

items.docs: Return the latency history for a client. Clients can be identified by a client key or either the MAC or IP depending on whether the network uses Track-by-IP. The latency data is from a sample of 2% of packets and is grouped into 4 traffic categories: background, best effort, video, voice. Within these categories the sampled packet counters are bucketed by latency in milliseconds.

items.docs: Query for details on the organization's RadSec device Certificate Authority certificates (CAs). The primary CA signs all the certificates that devices present when establishing a secure connection to RADIUS servers via RadSec protocol. This API returns an array of the status of all of the CAs as well as their contents, if they've been generated. An organization will have at most one CA unless the CA is being rotated.

info.name: Create an organization's RadSec device Certificate Authority (CA)

items.docs: Create an organization's RadSec device Certificate Authority (CA). Call this endpoint when turning on RadSec in the firmware for the first time. Calling this endpoint starts an asynchronous process to generate the CA; call GET afterwards to retrieve the contents of the CA. Note this CA is generated and controlled by Meraki. Subsequent calls will not generate a new CA.

info.name: Update an organization's RadSec device Certificate Authority (CA) state

items.docs: Update an organization's RadSec device Certificate Authority (CA) state. Note this CA is generated and controlled by Meraki. Call this endpoint to update the state to "trusted", at which point Meraki will generate device certificates. "trusted" means the CA is placed on your RadSec server(s) and devices establishing a secure connection using certs signed by this CA will pass verification.

params.description: Optional parameter to filter the result set by the included set of network IDs

params.name: serials
params.description: A list of serial numbers. The returned devices will be filtered to only include these serials.

params.name: bssids
params.description: A list of BSSIDs. The returned devices will be filtered to only include these BSSIDs.

params.name: hideDisabled
params.description: If true, the returned devices will not include disabled SSIDs. (default: true)

params.name: perPage
params.description: The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 500. Default is 100.

params.name: startingAfter
params.description: A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.

params.name: endingBefore
params.description: A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.
